subject: Geopolitics
title: Stanislav Petrov's Decision
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Stanislav Petrov's Decision.

hook.text: September 26, 1983. Soviet sensors reported five US missiles incoming. Lieutenant Colonel Petrov had minutes to decide.

buildup.text: Protocol demanded Petrov report the launch to his superiors. They would likely authorize a full retaliatory strike.

discovery.text: Petrov judged it a false alarm. Five missiles made no sense for a real first strike. He reported a system error.

twist.text: He was right. Sunlight reflecting off high-altitude clouds had fooled the satellite sensors. It was a glitch.

climax.text: One man trusted his judgment over the machines. That decision may have prevented the deaths of hundreds of millions.

punchline.text: The world was saved by a gut feeling, not a system.

quiz.question: Why did Petrov doubt the missile warning?
options: The warning came from an unreliable ally
Five missiles made no sense for a real first strike
He had received advance notice of a test
